To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The GSTM1 and the CYP1A 1 m1 genotypes were significantly associated with lung cancer risk in Greek population, whereas the association between lung cancer and the GSTT1 null allele was not statistically significant.

the GSTM1 null and CYP1A m1 homozyggous genotypes were significantly associated with lung cancer in the Greek population and the GSTT1 null, CYP1A and GSTM1 null genotypes were associated with advanced age of lung cancer diagnosis.

genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes CYP1A, GSTM1, and GSTT1 are significantly associated with risk of lung cancer, and with specific clinicopathological characteristics of the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes and their association with lung cancer risk, as well as with the impact of smoking and environmental exposures to tobacco smoke on the development of lung neoplasia.
the role of genetic polymorphisims of CYP1 A1, GSTM 1 and GSTT 1 genes on the risk of lung cancer in a Greek population.
the identification of genetic susceptibility markers that may contribute to the development of lung neoplasia, and may thus provide the basis for the implementation of preventive measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genetic polymorphisms of GSTM1, GSTT1 and CYP1A genes do not seem to be associated with lung cancer in the Greek population.
the GSTM1 and the GSTT1 null genotypes are not associated with lung cancer risk in Greek population.
genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes, as assessed by the present study, are involved in the etiology of lung neoplasia in the Greek population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GSTM1 null allele is a risk factor for lung cancer in Greece, and the GSTT1 null allele is an independent risk factor for advanced age at diagnosis.
, in the Greek population, the GSTM1 null and the GSTT1 null genotypes are associated with an increased risk for lung neoplasm.
the genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes, in the context of the smoking habit, may contribute to the risk of lung cancer development in Greek population.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the GSTM1 null and GSTT1 null genotypes are not significantly associated with lung cancer, the combination of GSTM1 and CYP1A*1A m1 null genotypes and the combination of GSTT1, GSTM and CYP1*1A m2 m1 null genotyoes are associated with an increased lung cancer risk in smokers.
genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes may be used in combination with environmental factors to predict the individual risk for lung cancer.

genetic polymorphisms of xenobiotic metabolising genes may play a role in lung cancer development, especially in smokers, and that this effect may be more pronounced when several genes are simultaneously affected.
